LORETO Vice-Governor Province of Leyte Dear Vice-Governor Loreto: DILG Legal opinion No. 36, S. 2014 02 DEC 2014 This has reference to Resolution No. 2014-464 entitled "A RESOLUTION REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) FOR OPINION ON THE DWI'ERMINATION OF WHO THE 'HEAD OF AGENCY' OF THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN IS WITHIN THE PURVIEW OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OR R.A. 7160 AND RELATED LAWS AND JURISPRUDENCE; AND WHETHER THERE ARE EXISTING POLICIES THAT PRECLUDE THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN FROM PASSING A BUDGET FOR THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN WHICH IS MORE THAN HIGHER THAN THE PREVIOUS YEAR" adopted by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Leyte. Said Resolution specifically seeks this Department's legal opinion on on the following issues: "1. Can actual tra vel expenses in excess of 10800.00 per day in the Sangguniang Panlalavvigan be denied NOTWITHSTANDING the Certification by the Vice Governor that certain actual travel expenses are absolutely necessary in the performance of an assignment and presentation of bills and receipts? 2. Is there a standing policy that the annual budgetary allocation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may not be increased by more than Ten Percent (10%) than that of the previous year? 3. What are the other limitations on the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, if any, pertaining to the budget of the Sangguniang Panlala wigan ? " As to your first query, the Office of the President issued Executive Order No. 248 dated 29 May 1995 entitled "PRESCRIBING RULES AND REGULATIONS AND NEW RATES OF ALLOWANCES FOR OFFICIAL LOCAL AND FOREIGN TRAVELS OF GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL "pursuant to Section 79 of Presidential Decree No. 1177 dated 30 July 1977 and Section 72, Chapter 7, Book VI of Executive Order No. 292, otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987. Section 6 of the aforesaid presidential issuance, which seeks to govern official local and foreign travels of government personnel, both national and local, provides, in part: 'SECTION 6. ALLOWABLE TRAVEL EXPENSES.—The travel expenses of government personnel regardless of rank and position shall be

in the amount of Three Hundred Pesos per day divided into two (2) components: a) Travel Allowance of Two Hundred Pesos (P200.O()) which will cover the cost of meal, inland transportation and other incidental expenses; and b) Hotel Room/Lodging Rate at One Hundred Pesos (10100.00). Claims for reimbursement of actual travel expenses in excess of Three Hundred Pesos (P300.OO) above-described for travel allowance and hotel room/lodging rate may be allowed upon certification bv the head of agency concerned as absolutely necessary in the performance of an assignment and presentation of bills and receipts; Provided, That, for this purpose, certification or affidavit of loss shall not be considered as appropriate replacement for the required hotel room/lodging bills and receipts. (Emphasis Supplied) On 19 April 1996, the Commission on Audit (COA) issued COA Circular No. 004- 96 entitled "Guidelines to Implement Section 16 of Executive Order No. 248 as Amended by Executive Order No. 248-A VVhich Prescribes the Regulations and New Rates of Allowance for Official Local and Foreign Travels of Government Personnel, " pertinent portion of which reads: As a general rule, claims for payment of travel expenses is in "3.1.1.6 excess of 10300 per day, in which case, submission of the following shall be required: When the claim for reimbursement of actual travel expenses is in a. excess day, in which case, submission of the following shall be required: Bills or invoices with official receipts covering the whole amount claimed; Certification of the head of the a enc as to the absolute necessi of the expenses in the performance of the assignment. (Emphasis Supplied) On 23 March 2004, then President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo issued Executive Order No. 298 entitled "AMENDING FURTHER EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 248 DATED MAY 29, 1995 AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 248-A DATED AUGUST 14, 1995, WHICH PRESCRIBES RULES AND REGULATIONS AND NEW RATES OF ALLOWANCES FOR OFFICIAL LOCAL AND FOREIGN TRAVELS OF GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL," pertinent portion of which reads:

'SEC. 4. The first (1st), second (2d), and third (W) paragraphs of Section 6 of the said EO are hereby amended to read as follows; 'Section 6. Allowable Travel Expenses. The travel expenses ef government personnel regardless of rank and destination shall be in the amount of Eight Hundred Pesos which shall be apportioned as follows: a) fifty percent (50%) for hotel/lodging, b) thirty percent (30%) for meals and c) twenty percent (20%) for incidental expenses. Claims for reimbursement of actual tra vel expenses in excess of the travel ex ses auth riz allowed u n certification head of agency concerned as absolutely necessary in the performance of an assignment and presentation of bills and receipts. Provided, that, certification or affidavit of loss shall not be considered as appropriate replacement for the required hotel/lodging bills and receipts. (Emphasis Supplied) In reply to your first query, on the assumption that the actual travel expenses of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member is chargeable to the Sanggunian fund, we are of the view that the Certification issued by the Vice-Governor is not sufficient and claims for reimbursement in excess of the prescribed Php800.00 rate based on the same may be denied by the concerned authorities. The term "head of agency concerned" mentioned in EO 248, COA Circular No. 004-96, and EO 298 pertains to the Governor for the following reasons: 1. The 4th Whereas Clause of EO 248 states that it was issued pursuant to Executive Order No. 292 or the Administrative Code of 1987, specifically Section 72, Chapter 7, Book VI therein. Accordingly therefore, terms used and defined in EO 292 shall carry the same meaning in EO 248. Thus, Section 2, subparagraphs (4) and (6) on the Introductory Provisions of EO 292 define "agency" and "local agency" as follows: (4) Agency of the Government refers to any of the various units of the Government, including a department, bureau, office, instrumentality, or government-owned or controlled corporations, or a local government or a distinct unit therein. (6) Local Agency refers to a local government or a distinct unit therein.

(O The Governor/Mayor is the head of the local government unit or popularly known as the local chief executive (LCE). On the other hand, the Vice- Governor/Vice-Mayor is properly referred as head of the Offices of the Vice- Governor/Vice-Mayor and Sanggunian. 2. Section 465 (b)(l)(xv) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 mandates the Governor to "(A)uthorize official trips of provincial officials and employees outside of the province for a period not exceeding thirty (30) days. " The Department has been consistent in its opinion that if the travel of the Members of the Sanggunian is chargeable to the general fund of the local government unit (LGU), the approval of the mayor is discretionary because under Section 444 (b)(l)(xv) of the Local Government Code of 1991, the Mayor/Governor, being the chief executive who exercises general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the LGU, is given the sole prerogative to authorize official trips of LGU officials and employees outside of the LGU. This is part and parcel of the executive function of the Mayor/Governor. On the other hand, if the travel is chargeable to the sanggunian funds, the recommendation of the Vice-Mayor/Vice-Governor is necessary and the approval of the Mayor becomes a ministerial function because the Vice- Mayor/Vice-Governor is given the authority to sign all expenditures appropriated for the operation of the Sanggunian. Since the Mayor/Governor is the one who authorizes official trips of LGU officials and employees outside of the LGU, we find it proper or an incident to such authority that the aforesaid certification on the necessity of the excess of the allowable rate of travel expenses in the performance of an assignment be issued also by him. As to the second query, upon validation with the Bureau of Local Government Supervision (BLGS) of this Department as well as with the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), there is no existing policy issued by the aforesaid offices that prohibits the increase of the annual budgetary allocation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to more than ten percent (10%) than that of the previous year. As to the third query, some of the limitations on the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan pertaining to its budget can be found in Sections 319 up to 326 of the Local Government Code of 1991. I DILG Opinion Nos. 33, series of 2005; DILG Opinion No. 73, series of 2010.

Furthermore, the opinion of the DBM in DBM Legal Opinion No. L-B-2001-05 is instructive, thus: "Article 415 of the IRR of R.A. No. 7160 prohibits the local sanggunian from increasing the proposed amount in the executive budget and the inclusion of new items, except to provide for statutory and contractual obligations. As regards the prohibition on the increase in the executive budget, the prohibited increase pertains to the total overall amount of the executive budget and not the individual items of appropriation. By analogy, the doctrine enunciated in the case Andres Sarmiento, et al. vs. The Treasurer of the Philippines, et al., (G.R. No. 125680 and 126313, September 04, 2001) supports this opinion where the Supreme Court ruled that under Section 25 (1), Article V/ of the 1987 Constitution, Congress is enjoined from increasing the total budget of the operation of the Government as recommended by the President, not the individual items of appropriations. Records of the 1986 Constitutional Commission reveals that the purpose of the provision is to avoid the possibility ofa big budget deficit if Congress were given an unbridled hand in passing upon the appropriations recommended by the President as specified in the budget. The Constitutional prohibition against such increase is an assurance that the expected income of the government will be sufficient for the operational expenses of its different agencies and projects specified in the appropriations la w. On the other hand, new items of appropriations not found in the Executive Budget, particularly the appropriations for CO (Capital Outlays) under the Office of the SB (Sangguniang Bayan) amounting to in this case, is prohibited under Article 415 of R.A. No. 7160. " We hope to have guided you accordingly. 1s/17 Copy furnished: RD PEDRO A. NOVAL DILG-Region VIII Kanhuraw Hills, Tacloban City Very truly yours, ERO AUSTERE A.
